title: August and the Smile
premise: Freya Oyelaran takes a teaching post in the frost-bound village of Hollowmere, where a class of children has been missing since 1911 and the school's records refuse to say why. When the church bell—melted down over a century ago—begins ringing at night, Freya realizes the village made a bargain to keep the cold out, and the debt is coming due. As the frost spreads patterns across every window and the missing class returns to sit silently at their desks, Freya must choose between the villagers' duty of silence and the truth that could free them. In the end, Freya breaks the seal by reading the 1911 register aloud at dawn, unmaking the invitation—but not before losing someone they have come to love.
about_author: Casper Almeida is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who spent six years in villages where the winters outlasted the residents. They write horror about institutions, ledgers, and the things communities agree not to write down.

chapters.title: The Register
chapters.summary: Freya arrives in Hollowmere by the last bus before the roads close, finding a school with eleven desks but registers listing twenty-two pupils. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: cautious hope curdling into unease as the headteacher warns them never to teach after dark.

chapters.title: Eleven Empty Chairs
chapters.summary: On the first morning, eleven chairs are warm though no one sat in them. Freya begins documenting everything—their 'prayer'—while the caretaker, Ivo, quietly moves the chairs back each evening. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: the comfort of routine against the first crack in rational explanation.

chapters.title: What the Bell Was Melted For
chapters.summary: In the parish archive, Freya finds the 1911 record: the bell was melted to make eleven small bells, one for each child lost to the winter. The ledger page after that is burned away. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: scholarly fascination shading into dread.

chapters.title: Ivo
chapters.summary: Ivo tends the school boiler like a vigil, feeding it through nights when the temperature shouldn't allow fire. He tells Freya the village keeps the cold 'polite,' and asks nothing else. POV: alternating Freya and Ivo. Emotional beat: two lonely people recognizing each other; the first tenderness.

chapters.title: First Ringing
chapters.summary: At 3 a.m. the church bell rings—a bell that is slag in a scrapyard. The whole village stands in doorways, heads bowed, until it stops. No one will speak of it. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: isolation deepening; the village closes like a fist.

chapters.title: The Frost Writes
chapters.summary: Frost patterns appear on the classroom windows spelling half-formed names. Freya photographs them; by morning the photos show only blank glass. The documentation-prayer fails for the first time. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: the terror of being disbelieved even by one's own evidence.

chapters.title: The Mothers' Circle
chapters.summary: Village matriarch Sefu Halloway invites Freya to tea and explains the covenant obliquely: something was invited in during the hungry winter of 1911 to spare the living, and invitations can be renewed—or refused. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: seduction of belonging offered at a terrible price.

chapters.title: Attendance
chapters.summary: The register now lists twelve names. A new pupil, pale and punctual, sits in the twelfth desk and answers roll in a voice like snow settling. Freya marks her present because refusing feels fatal. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: complicity—the first corruption of power's smallest form, a teacher's pen.

chapters.title: Ivo's Confession
chapters.summary: Ivo reveals his family has fed the boiler for four generations; the fire isn't for warmth but for keeping the invited thing 'at the threshold.' His line ends with him. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: inherited duty as a cage; he looks at Freya and wants, for once, to be free.

chapters.title: The Missing Class Returns
chapters.summary: During a whiteout, the eleven children of 1911 file into the classroom and take their seats, frost blooming from their breath. They do not harm anyone. They simply wait for a lesson. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: pity overriding fear—they are hostages too.

chapters.title: Sefu's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sefu offers Freya a place in the Mothers' Circle: sign the renewal, gain belonging, safety, and Ivo's protection. The alternative, she implies, is joining the register. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized—power corrupts precisely by making refusal feel like suicide.

chapters.title: What Was Invited
chapters.summary: In the burned ledger's surviving fragments, Freya reconstructs the truth: the village invited the Frost itself inside to kill the fever of 1911, and it took the children as interest. It has been renewing its lease ever since. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: revelation as grief—the protectors were the perpetrators.

chapters.title: Renewal Night
chapters.summary: The village gathers to sign the covenant; the bell rings them in. Freya attends, pen in hand, and watches neighbors sign with relief and shame. At the last moment Freya does not sign. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: the loneliest act of courage—public refusal.

chapters.title: Consequences
chapters.summary: The village turns on Freya: supplies withheld, the bus road closed, the classroom locked. The twelfth pupil appears at Freya's lodgings window each night, closer each time. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: siege; belonging revoked becomes punishment.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Pupil
chapters.summary: Freya finally speaks to the girl—Edith, first name on the 1911 list—and learns the children are held as collateral, conscious, waiting for someone to read their names back into the world. Reading the register aloud would void the invitation. Or end the reader. POV: Edith. Emotional beat: hope kindled in the dark.

chapters.title: Ivo's Choice
chapters.summary: Ivo lets the boiler die. Without the fire, the Frost presses fully against the threshold, and the village panics. He chooses Freya over his inheritance, knowing what it costs. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: love against duty, stated plainly at last.

chapters.title: The Longest Night
chapters.summary: Winter solstice. The Frost writes its final pattern across every surface in town, a signature completing itself. The villagers, freezing, realize the covenant was always a loan, never a gift. Some come to Freya's door. POV: multiple villagers. Emotional beat: collective reckoning; pride breaking into plea.

chapters.title: Reading Aloud
chapters.summary: At midnight Freya enters the frozen schoolhouse, opens the 1911 register, and begins reading the eleven names aloud while the Frost unmakes the room around them. Each name spoken returns a child a little more to warmth. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: documentation fulfilled as true prayer—naming as rescue.

chapters.title: The Price of the Pen
chapters.summary: The Frost demands a name in exchange for the eleven. Ivo speaks his own before Freya can, stepping into the pattern. The bell rings once, softly, and goes silent forever. POV: Ivo, then Freya. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the answer to corruption—power renounced, love kept.

chapters.title: Sunrise
chapters.summary: Dawn comes late and clean. The frost patterns melt into ordinary water. The eleven children are gone—not taken, released—and the twelfth desk stands empty with a single pressed flower on it. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: exhausted, wounded peace.

chapters.title: After the Thaw
chapters.summary: Spring. Freya stays to teach a real class of nine living children, and rewrites the school's history honestly in a new register. The village, diminished and ashamed, begins again. Sefu brings bread to the doorstep—an apology without words. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: belonging rebuilt on truth instead of silence.

chapters.title: August
chapters.summary: Years later, in August, Freya finds a small bell on the schoolhouse step, warm to the touch despite the heat, engraved with Ivo's initials. It rings once, gently, like a greeting. Freya smiles, hangs it by the door, and opens the school. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: mourning transmuted into continuance; love outlasting duty.
